title: 1963 AHSME Problem 7
statement:
Given the four equations:

\[ \begin{aligned} (1)\quad&3y-2x=12,\\ (2)\quad&-2x-3y=10,\\ (3)\quad&3y+2x=12,\\ (4)\quad&2y+3x=10. \end{aligned} \]

The pair representing perpendicular lines is:

solutions.text:
Line \((1)\) has slope \(\frac{2}{3},\) and line \((4)\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{2}.\) Their product is \(-1,\) so these two lines are perpendicular.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Rewrite each equation in slope-intercept form
Perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is \(-1\)
